[[File:Murk-TEA.jpg|thumb|250px|[[Murk (star)|Murk]], a red dwarf in the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]].]]
A '''red dwarf''' was a type of [[Dwarf star/Legends|dwarf star]]. [[Color/Legends|Red]] dwarfs, similar to [[Brown dwarf/Legends|brown dwarfs]], did not have enough [[Fuel/Legends|fusion fuel]] at the beginning of their existence to become larger [[Star/Legends|stars]], and gave off light comparable to an average [[Moon/Legends|moon]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Red dwarfs made up some 70 percent of the stars in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and had a very low chance of supporting indigenous life and tended to be uninhabited. The [[Manda sector/Legends|Manda sector]], for instance, had some 84 inhabited [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], but 344 red dwarf systems. Most red dwarf systems were cursorily surveyed by [[Probe droid/Legends|probots]] in the early years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and were left alone unless they appeared to have exploitable resources. [[Barab (star)/Legends|Barab]] was a rare red dwarf that supported native life, the [[Barabel/Legends|Barabels]] of [[Barab I/Legends|Barab I]].<ref name="TEA" />

Red dwarfs were often companions to other stars, and any [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] red dwarfs were likely to be small terrestrial worlds. Such planets tended to have minimal [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]], but potentially could contain mineral deposits of some value or rarity, or unusual [[Ore/Legends|ores]].<ref name="GG8">''[[Galaxy Guide 8: Scouts]]''</ref>
